quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When a stop is required at an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk markings, what should a driver do?

options.text: You do not have to stop.
You must slow down to make sure crossing traffic is clear.
You should stop where you can see at least 200 feet on both sides, even if you enter the intersecting roadway.
You should stop where you can clearly see approaching traffic before entering the intersecting roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should stop where you can clearly see approaching traffic before entering the intersecting roadway.
questions.explanation: With no stop line or crosswalk, stop as close to the intersecting roadway as possible where you can see traffic coming. Do not enter the intersecting roadway just to get a better view.

questions.question: What should you do before leaving the interstate?

options.text: Signal and move to the correct lane at least one mile before your exit.
Slow down to 45 miles per hour before reaching your exit.
Signal and slow down 50 to 100 feet before entering the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and move to the correct lane at least one mile before your exit.
questions.explanation: Plan ahead and watch for exit signs. Get into the correct lane at least one mile before your exit. Do not slow down until after you move into the exit ramp.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the roadway.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: Chevron signs show the direction of a sharp curve. The arrow points the way the road turns. You may see several of these signs throughout a curve.

questions.question: What is important to do before turning left?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Yield to oncoming vehicles.
Swing to the right side of your lane.
Wait until oncoming traffic has a red light.

questions.explanation: When turning left at a traffic signal, you must let pedestrians and oncoming traffic go first.

questions.question: You see a steady yellow traffic light ahead and have not entered the intersection yet. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get through before the red light.
Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.explanation: A yellow light means get ready to stop. If you are already in the intersection, leave as quickly as you can.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic signal ahead.
Fire station.
T intersection.
Left turn signal.

questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you a traffic light is coming. Be ready to stop for a red light or slow for a yellow light. Watch for cross traffic.

questions.question: If an oncoming vehicle uses high beams, where should you look?

options.text: Either side of the road
The center of the road
The right side of the road
The left side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side of the road
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded by the other vehicle's lights. This lets you stay on your road safely until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: If you are about to be hit from behind, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Release your seat belt.
Brace yourself.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.explanation: Keep your seat belt on. Push back against your seat and press your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to brake if you are pushed toward another vehicle.

questions.question: You are in the center lane of an expressway and cars keep passing you on both sides. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the right lane.
Move to the left lane.

questions.explanation: On highways with four or more lanes, use the right lanes unless you are passing or turning left. If you are driving slower than traffic flow, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: How can you check your blind spots when changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Use the outside rearview mirror.
Use both the inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Always turn your head to check your blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, how can you avoid traffic merging from on-ramps on your right?

options.text: Change lanes to the left.
Slow down.
Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.explanation: When you see an on-ramp ahead on an interstate, move to the left lane when it is safe. This lets vehicles merge from the on-ramp without problems.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, what should you usually do?

options.text: Go slowly and wait for an opening.
Speed up faster than other traffic.
Turn on your hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.
Speed up to match the freeway traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the freeway traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up and match the freeway traffic speed. This helps you merge in safely and smoothly. Remember that you must yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: Why should you be alert to motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
They rarely use their headlights.
Motorcycle riders are less skilled than other drivers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are smaller and easier to miss than cars. They can hide in your blind spot. It is also hard to judge how far away a motorcycle is or how fast it is going. Always watch carefully for motorcycles.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill by a curb, turn your steering wheel away from the curb. If your car rolls, it will roll into the curb and stay in place.

questions.question: When passing a bicycle, how much clearance must you provide?

options.text: One foot
Two feet
Three feet
Five feet

questions.explanation: The law requires at least three feet of space when passing a bicycle. Keep this distance until you are completely past the bicycle.

questions.question: What is true about a work zone?

options.text: It may be moving or stationary.
It is marked with black and white signs.
You do not need to slow down or pay extra attention.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may be moving or stationary.
questions.explanation: Work zones can be in one place or moving. They may include lane striping, mowing, or snow removal. Work zones have orange signs with black letters. Always slow down and pay close attention in work zones.

questions.question: What does this yellow warning sign mean?

options.text: You are approaching a school or school crosswalk.
Slow down, drive with care, and watch for children.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a school or school crosswalk is nearby. Slow down, be careful, and look for children.

questions.question: You must give the right-of-way to any pedestrian who is:

options.text: In a marked crosswalk.
In any crosswalk or intersection.
Crossing any street.

questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians crossing in marked or unmarked crosswalks. For safety, yield to anyone crossing the street.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Drive with care and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
Stop completely and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down, be ready to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be ready to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means yield. Slow down when you see it and be ready to stop. Let other vehicles, bicycles, or people pass safely before you go.

questions.question: What is the speed limit on a dirt county road if no other speed limit is posted?

options.text: 40 miles per hour.
45 miles per hour.
50 miles per hour.

questions.explanation: The normal speed limit on a dirt county road is 50 miles per hour. Follow any posted speed limit signs if they show a different speed.

questions.question: You see a steady yellow light at an intersection ahead. You have not entered the intersection yet. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to pass through before the red light.
Slow down and carefully drive through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means you should stop safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through at a safe speed.

questions.question: You see heavy smoke ahead on the road. What should you do?

options.text: Turn on your flashers and keep driving.
Slow down, move to the right, and stop away from the road.
Turn on your high beams and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to the right, and stop away from the road.
questions.explanation: When you see heavy smoke ahead, slow down right away. Move to the right and stop off the road. Only continue if it is safe. Some smoke can harm your eyes, lungs, or be dangerous.

questions.question: The Child Passenger Restraint Law requires children up to age ____ to use a federally-approved child safety seat.

options.text: Four
Six
Eight

questions.explanation: Children up to age six must sit in a federally-approved child safety seat when riding in a vehicle.

questions.question: How do you avoid glare from oncoming headlights?

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Look at the centerline of the road.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look briefly to the right side of the road to avoid the bright lights of an oncoming car. Then look ahead again to watch the other vehicle's position.

questions.question: Your vehicle's stopping distance increases when stopping on:

options.text: A wet or icy road.
Paved highways.
At night.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stopping distance increases on wet or icy roads. It also increases on roads with loose gravel or stones.
